analysis.title: Gap Inc. (GAP): F3Q26 Earnings Review: Old Navy shows sequential progress but softer start to holiday drives reduced FY26 outlook
key_insights: GAP reported F3Q26 adjusted EPS of $0.82 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.77/$0.78. Consolidated comps were flat Y/Y, in line with GS and below consensus of +1.4%.
Brand comps: Gap +9%, Old Navy flat (vs -4% in F2Q), Banana Republic -3%, Athleta -15%.

Adjusted gross margin of 42.4% missed GS/consensus of 42.9%/43.0%. SG&A leveraged about 130bps Y/Y, mainly on lower incentive compensation, so adjusted operating margin of 9.8% beat GS/consensus of 9.3%/9.4%.

Management said Old Navy was tracking ahead of expectations through September. Warm weather then pressured seasonal demand in October and early November. Recent trends recovered to roughly the F3Q rate as temperatures normalized.
The F4Q Old Navy comp guide of -1% to -2% includes the early-November pressure, roughly flat recent trends and a slight further improvement. Pent-up seasonal demand is upside not in guidance.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $2.29-$2.34 from $2.35-$2.45, vs GS/FactSet consensus of $2.42/$2.39.

FY26 net sales are now guided to roughly flat Y/Y (from +1.0%-1.5%). Adjusted operating margin is now about 7.2% (from about 7.4%-7.6%). Adjusted gross margin is now down slightly Y/Y (from up slightly).

An updated tariff assumption adds about $46mn to FY gross profit and operating income, or about 30bps of margin. Incremental promotion at Old Navy and Athleta and the slower start to F4Q still lowered the margin outlook.
F4Q guidance: net sales down 1% to flat vs GS/consensus of +3.4%/+3.1%. Gross margin 38.0%-38.3% vs 39.5%/39.2%. Implied adjusted EPS $0.56-$0.61 vs consensus $0.74/$0.71.
Athleta named Ashley Kechter Brand President and CEO effective December 14, and the company is reviewing the business. GS sees Athleta as a significant offset to sales and profit upside.

GS cut FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS estimates to $2.33/$2.45/$2.74 from $2.42/$2.69/$3.00. The reasons given were the F3Q result, a slower F4Q start, weaker Athleta trends and Banana Republic womenswear execution issues.
GS lowered its 12-month price target to $25 from $27 and kept the Buy rating. The target multiple on Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA fell to 4.00x from 4.35x. The stock was $18.79, implying 33% upside.
GS calls Old Navy a show-me story until it shows consistent positive comps and stronger merchandise margin. It says the result is soft but came against low investor expectations.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $25 from $27 on a lower 4.00x EV/EBITDA multiple (from 4.35x) after the FY26 guide cut. The Old Navy recovery is still unproven and Athleta remains weak.

earnings_insights: GAP F3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $0.82 (GAAP $0.86, including $0.04 of one-time items) vs GS consensus $0.77 and FactSet consensus $0.78, reported 11/19.
F3Q26 net sales rose 2% Y/Y vs GS/consensus of +1.9%/+1.8%. Total net sales were $4,011mn vs GS estimate $4,016mn.
F3Q26 adjusted gross margin was 42.4% vs GS/consensus estimates of 42.9%/43.0%. Adjusted operating margin was 9.8% vs GS/consensus estimates of 9.3%/9.4%.
Underlying merchandise margin rose 10bps excluding about 60bps of tariff benefit and about 30bps of fuel pressure.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance is $2.29-$2.34 (prior $2.35-$2.45) vs GS/FactSet consensus estimates of $2.42/$2.39.
F4Q26 implied adjusted EPS guidance is $0.56-$0.61 vs GS/FactSet consensus estimates of $0.74/$0.71.
GS FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS estimates are $2.33/$2.45/$2.74, from $2.42/$2.69/$3.00 prior.
Inventory fell 6.3% Y/Y vs a GS estimate of +1.3%. Cash was $2,578mn.
risk_factors: Long-term cost headwinds from freight and wage inflation pressuring margins.
Prolonged pressure on the low-income consumer's spending power.
Increased competition from off-price peers or other apparel businesses.
Athleta's continued weakness and the lengthy turnaround under new leadership.
Warm weather and promotions weighing on early F4Q trends at Old Navy.

tension_points.bull_case: Old Navy comps improved sequentially to flat in F3Q from -4% in F2Q. Recent trends recovered to roughly the F3Q rate after warm weather faded. Pent-up seasonal demand is upside not in the F4Q guide.
tension_points.bear_case: The F4Q Old Navy comp guide is -1% to -2%. Early-November weather pressure and incremental promotion cut the FY26 gross margin outlook. GS calls Old Navy a show-me story.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to return to positive, consistent comps with stronger merchandise margin. F4Q Old Navy comps weaker than the guided -1% to -2%.

theme_stances.key_argument: Sequential improvement at Old Navy is encouraging, but further improvement is needed to drive stock outperformance.
theme_stances.evidence: Old Navy brand remains a show-me story
